Surya @ Surja Sk vs New India Assurance Co. Ltd. & Anr on 8
May, 2025
 1
 In The High Court At Calcutta
 Civil Appellate Jurisdiction
 Appellate Side

Present:
The Hon'ble Justice Ananya Bandyopadhyay
 Fma 806 of 2023
 Surya @ Surja Sk.
 v.
 New India Assurance Co. Ltd. & Anr.

For the Appellants : Mr. Ashiq Mondal
 Mr. Sujit Islam
For the Respondents : Ms. Sucharita Paul
Heard on & Judgment on : 08.05.2025 Ananya Bandyopadhyay, J.:-
1.
The instant appeal was heard earlier and judgment was reserved.
However, the matter was listed under the heading "For Hearing" for further clarification.
2. The Learned Advocates representing the respective parties are present.

3. The claimant, Srya @ Surja Sk., filed an application under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal- cum-Judge, Special Court (EC Act), Berhampore,
Murshidabad, being M.A.C. Case No. 387 of 2015, seeking compensation of Rs. 8,49,500/- for injuries sustained in a road traffic accident that occurred on 19.02.2015 at about 12:00 Noon.

entities.text:
Motor Accident Claims Tribunal- cum-Judge, Special Court (EC Act), Berhampore,
Murshidabad
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: At the relevant time, the claimant was standing beside a motorcycle near Bostal Gate at Madhupur along N.H. 34, when a truck bearing Registration No. WB-23B-5791, being driven in a rash and negligent manner, dashed against him, causing grievous injuries.
The claimant was treated in various hospitals for the injuries sustained in the accident and claimed to have lost his earning capacity 4.
The owner of the offending vehicle appeared and filed a written objection but thereafter did not contest the case and the case proceeded ex parte against him.

New India Assurance Co. Ltd. & Anr.
contested the aforesaid MAC case.

5. The Learned Tribunal as aforesaid disposed of the issues framed considering the oral as well as documentary evidence and awarded a sum of Rs. 5,03,200/- as well as an interest of 5% from the date of filing the case till the realization of the amount.

Surya @ Surja Sk vs New India Assurance Co. Ltd. & Anr on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80004981/
1 6.

entities.text: Surya @ Surja Sk vs New India Assurance Co. Ltd. & Anr on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Learned Advocate representing the appellant/claimant submitted that the Learned Tribunal had erroneously considered the monthly income of the victim to be Rs. 4000/- and sought for enhancement of the same.
It was further submitted that a sum of 25% to be of the future prospect was not awarded.
It was further submitted for enhancing over a sum of Rs. 1,00,000/- should have been granted with regard to the element of pain and suffering towards medical treatment was not awarded.

Moreover, non pecuniary damages to the extent of 60% disability suffered by the victim as mentioned in the disability certificate marked as Ext.4 issued by the Medical Board Murshidabad Medical Collage and Hospital was not considered.

entities.text: Medical Board Murshidabad Medical Collage and Hospital
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
7. The Learned Advocate representing the respondent No.1/insurance company controverted the submissions of the learned Advocate representing the appellants/claimants stating that the learned Tribunal had rightly assessed the compensation awarded on the following grounds:
a.
The victim was a temporary' employee of 'Murshidabad District Truck Driver and Helper Shramik Union'.
The General Secretary of the, said Union, while deposing as PW4, before the Ld. Tribunal, confirmed the 'temporary employment' of the victim.
It was further stated by PW4 that the victim received a sum of Rs. 7,000/- per month as salary from the said Union.
In support of the above, PW4 produced one Income Certificate' issued by him on 25.03.2015, in favour of the victim, after his accident on 09.02.2015.
b. PW4 however, could not produce register or voucher before the Ld. Tribunal to show that the injured claimant was receiving Rs. 7,000/-per month.
(Page 17 of pbk) from the Union.

Therefore,
the Ld. Tribunal rightly assessed the compensation on the basis of income of Rs. 4,000/- per month (page 21 of pbk).
c. The Medical Board of Murshidabad Medical College & Hospital, issued the Disability Certificate in favour of the victim.

entities.text: Medical Board of Murshidabad Medical College & Hospital
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: From the said "Disability Certificate' (exhibit 4) it was found that the victim suffered 60% 'permanent disability/loss of earning capacity' due to the above accident.
Accordingly, the Ld. Tribunal computed the compensation on the basis of 60% loss of earning capacity of the victim.

The Insurance Company submits that the Id. Tribunal Judge was correct in considering the permanent disability' as well as 'functional disability' of the victim at 60%,
in accordance with the Certificate issued by the Medical Board and such assessment is as per settled principles of law [page 47-pbk-Disability Certificate).
d.
The claimant had produced some bills and prescriptions in connection with his treatment.
The said documents were marked 'Y' (series) for identification.
However, admittedly the claimant failed to prove any of the said documents in accordance with the settled principles of law.

The said fact was also confirmed in the award passed by the Ld. Tribunal (Page 21 para 4 of pbk).
e.

It is the well settled principle of law that when a document is produced before a Ld. Court, the same should be proved by its author or the authorized representative of the author of the concerned document.
Most importantly some of the 'medical bills' and 'cash memos' which were produced before the Ld. Tribunal, were of the years 2019, 2020 and 2021, i.e. 5/6 years after the accident dated 19.02.2015.
(From page 52 to page 66 of pbk).

There is no cogent evidence to prove the nexus between the treatment of the victim after his accident on 19.02.2015 and the bills' and 'cash memos,
Surya @ Surja Sk vs New India Assurance Co. Ltd. & Anr on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/80004981/
2 issued between 2019 to 2021.

entities.text: Surya @ Surja Sk vs New India Assurance Co. Ltd. & Anr on 8 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Accordingly, the said bills/cash memos' cannot be considered at all.

8. Considered the submission of the Learned Advocates representing both the parties.
9.

Since the occurrence of the accident, the driving license and other ancillary issues have not been disputed by the learned advocate representing the appellant/claimant, this Court restricts itself only to the points agitated by the Learned Advocate representing the appellant/claimant as well as respondent No.1/insurance company.

10. Considering the observations of the Hon'ble Apex Court in National insurance company Ltd. Vs.
Pranay Shetty & Anr1 and Sarala Verma & Ors. Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation & Anr.2 The impugned award of Rs. 05,03,200/- is modified as follows:

 Future Prospect (25%) Rs. 1000/-
 Rs. 5000/-

Annual income (Rs. 5000 x 12) Rs. 60,000/-
 Rs. 8,40,000/-
 Permanent disability 60% Rs. 5,04,000/-
 Pain & Suffering Rs. 1,00,000/-
 Pain & suffering, loss of amenities, Rs. 4,00,000/-
 And other non pecuniary damages  Rs. 10,04,000/
 Less  Rs. 5,03,200/-
 Entitlement  Rs. 3,99,200/-
 11.

The Learned Advocate for the appellant/claimant submitted   appellant/claimant has withdrawn a sum of Rs. 5,03,200 appellant/claimant is entitled to a sum of Rs. 3,99,200/- along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum to be paid from the date of filing of the claim application till the date of realization.
1 2017(4)TAC 673(S.C) (2009) 6 SC 121 12.

The Learned Advocate for the respondent No.1/insurance company is to deposit the balance sum of Rs. 3,99,200/- along with interest as aforesaid before the office of the learned Registrar General High Court at Calcutta within six weeks from the date of passing of this order.

entities.text: Registrar General High Court at Calcutta
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
13. The office of the Registrar General, High Court, Calcutta shall encash the said cheque and,
thereafter, disburse the same to the present appellant/claimant as mentioned by the Learned Judge,

3 being MAC Case No. 387 of 2015 on proof of proper identification of the appellant /claimant subject to payment of ad valorem Court's fees within four weeks.

15. The pending applications, if any, stands disposed of.
16. Copy of the order be sent to the Department as well as the concerned tribunal as expeditiously as possible.
